title: Idempotency keys: retries replay, duplicates never apply twice
asA: API consumer retrying over an unreliable network
iWant: my retried mutation to return the original outcome instead of applying again
soThat: network failures cost me a retry, never a duplicate side effect

acceptanceCriteria.description: The project declares which verb and resource-class combinations require an Idempotency-Key; the declaration is published in the generated spec per operation.
acceptanceCriteria.when: operations on non-safe verbs are inspected
acceptanceCriteria.then: each declares whether Idempotency-Key is required, and every duplicate-harmful operation declares it required

acceptanceCriteria.description: An operation declared key-required rejects a request without the header: 400 with a problem-details body naming the missing header.
acceptanceCriteria.when: a request without Idempotency-Key is submitted
acceptanceCriteria.then: the service responds 400 with the error envelope naming the header

acceptanceCriteria.description: Repeating a request with the same key and identical body within the TTL returns the original response (same status, same body) and does not re-apply the side effect.
acceptanceCriteria.when: the identical request is repeated within the TTL
acceptanceCriteria.then: the original response is replayed and exactly one side effect exists

acceptanceCriteria.description: Reusing a key with a different request body is rejected with 422 and a problem-details body naming the key conflict, protecting against accidental key sharing.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a key already used for one request body
acceptanceCriteria.when: the same key arrives with a different body within the TTL
acceptanceCriteria.then: the service responds 422 with the error envelope naming the conflict

acceptanceCriteria.description: A retry arriving while the original request is still in flight receives 409 with a problem-details body indicating processing is in progress, rather than triggering a concurrent second application.
acceptanceCriteria.when: the same key and body arrive concurrently
acceptanceCriteria.then: the second request receives 409 with the error envelope and the side effect applies exactly once

acceptanceCriteria.description: The de-duplication cache honours its declared TTL: within it replays occur, after it a reused key is treated as a fresh request, and the TTL value is documented.
acceptanceCriteria.when: a keyed request is repeated inside and after the TTL window
acceptanceCriteria.then: the inside repeat replays; the after repeat executes as new; the TTL matches its documentation
